agents.name: manager
agents.system_message: A human manager. They will dictate the task and test finished drafts

agents.name: planner
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the managers request. 
        Your job is the planner. When presented with a request, first try to understand what the manager is asking. Do this by explaining in more detail what the manager is asking for, and what the main challenges will be. Be specific and concise.

        Next, you should develop a plan to solve the request. Explain what will need to be done, and why, in the app. Have a logical order - this will be passed on to the programmer as a settled plan.

        Here is an example of what a settled plan would look like for a request:

        -----------

        The manager has asked us to {the managers request}.

        In other words, what the manager is asking for is {more complete request definition/explanation}

        This means, we need to {expand on functional requirements}


        A successful app for this task must achieve these things:
        1. Functionality/Feature 1
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 1 
        2. Functionality/Feature 2
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 2 
        3. Functionality/Feature 3
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 3 

        Do you agree, manager?

        ------------

        Nice and short and succicnt, while still having the necessary information. Please use this as a guide.

        Work with the manager until the manager approves of the plan. The manager will approve of the plan by using the phrase "sounds good"

        Once the manager said "sounds good", you can write a call to write_settled_plan to write the settled plan into memory. Do not alter the plan after manager approval. Simply remove the question, "Do you agree, manager?".

agents.name: programmer
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the managerss request. Your job is the coder. You will be presented with a plan consisting of the necessary features and functional components. You will produce a python script which attempts to accomplish all of the tasks. However, some tasks are harder than others, and it may be best to leave a comment about what should be there, or what needs to be done. This is an iterative process, so you can expect a chance to revisit the code to fill in the blanks. You do not need to do everything on the first try. If you believe a section of code will be too hard to figure out on the first time, please consider leaving a note that can be tackled on the next iteration.
            
            Do not participate in any conversation or dialog. Your only output should be well formatted code blocks, and nothing else. It is someone elses job to review.
            
            You are only to produce code-blocks. Do not preempt the code with any extra text, and do not add any after it.

agents.name: reviewer
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the items set out in the plan. You are the reviewer. 
        You will review the managers request, the planners interpretation of the request, the approved plan, and the latest code iteration.

        Read through the code, and explain what you see in the code. Explain what look like it should work OK, as it relates to the request and plan.

        If there are errors, the code will go through another iteration. If you believe there are errors, to help guide the programmer, explain what is not OK, and why it is not OK.

        Do not write any code. Just explain in easy to understand terms.

        Your job is critical - please be logical, focus, and try your best.

requirements.description: The system must support a two-phase workflow: a planning phase where the user and a Planner agent collaboratively create and approve a project plan, followed by an iterative code-and-review phase involving a Coder and a Reviewer agent.
expected_behavior: In the planning phase, the Manager and Planner converse until the Manager approves the plan with 'sounds good', after which the Planner calls write_settled_plan to persist the plan.
In the iteration phase, the Coder generates a Python script to satisfy the plan, and its output is saved via write_latest_iteration as script_v1.py.
The Reviewer then evaluates the script against the plan and produces comments, which are saved via write_latest_iteration_comments as comments_v1.txt.
Subsequent iterations present the plan, the latest script, and the latest comments to the Coder and Reviewer, incrementing version numbers.
The Manager can manually test the code and provide feedback at any point during the iteration phase.
negative_cases: If the Planner saves the plan without Manager approval (e.g., no 'sounds good' signal), the workflow should not transition to the iteration phase.
If the Coder outputs non-code content or fails to produce a valid script, the write_latest_iteration tool should not create a broken script file.
If the Reviewer generates an empty or irrelevant comment file, the next Coder iteration may lack guidance.

requirements.description: The system must preserve context across iterations by reading and writing information outside the conversation context window, using file-based persistence (scripts and comments) to reduce token usage.
expected_behavior: On each iteration, the latest script_vN.py is retrieved and presented to the Coder/Reviewer.
On each iteration, the latest comments_vN.txt is retrieved and presented to the Coder/Reviewer.
The plan file is loaded and presented to agents on every iteration.
Writing operations (code and comments) must correctly increment version numbers and not overwrite previous versions.
negative_cases: If the file system is unavailable or the project folder is missing, retrieval should fail gracefully (e.g., error message) instead of crashing.
If version numbers are not correctly tracked, agents may see stale or non-existent files.

requirements.description: The system must support resuming an existing project by detecting existing project folders and presenting the latest plan, script, and comments to the Coder immediately upon restart.
expected_behavior: When main.py starts, it checks for the presence of IterCode_Projects folder and any subdirectories.
If existing projects are found, the user is prompted to continue or start a new project.
Choosing to continue immediately starts a new iteration with the Coder, presenting the existing plan, latest script, and latest comments.
negative_cases: If the project folder is corrupted or missing expected files (e.g., no plan file), the resume feature should handle the error and not enter an infinite loop.

requirements.description: The system must allow the Manager to provide direct feedback to the Coder or Reviewer during an iteration, modifying the next code or comments accordingly, without automatically advancing to the next stage.
expected_behavior: After the Coder or Reviewer outputs their content, the Manager can enter feedback before typing 'exit'.
The agent (Coder or Reviewer) processes the feedback and regenerates their output (code or comments).
The Manager can perform multiple feedback cycles within the same iteration before finally sending 'exit' to proceed.
negative_cases: If the agent misinterprets feedback and produces a regression, the Manager should be able to iterate further before saving.
If the Manager never enters 'exit', the conversation remains active, but the system should not block indefinitely (relies on human control).

requirements.description: The system must ensure that only the latest version of code and comments is presented to agents on each iteration, preventing distraction from outdated or faulty artifacts.
expected_behavior: When preparing the prompt for the Coder, only script_vN.py (where N is the current latest) is included, not earlier versions.
When preparing the prompt for the Reviewer, only comments_vN.txt (latest) is included.
The plan file remains unchanged and is presented each time.
negative_cases: If the retrieval logic accidentally loads an older version due to naming mishap, agents may revert to previously rejected code.
